data.text:
The Politics of Revenge: Sara Duterte’s Road to Malacañang

Some people asked me recently if Sara Duterte is indeed vengeful. I answered with a resounding YES. How she reacted to circumstances brought upon by the confidential fund fiasco, the killer instinct displayed in one of her press briefings, and of course, Zuleika Lopez. Who could ever forget how she went berserk and threatened the President, the First Lady, and former Speaker Martin Romualdez.

Romualdez, her nemesis, to which she blames all her political misfortunes. The Speaker who stood in her way of becoming President in the soonest possible time, the one who moved heaven and earth to protect the Filipinos from the dangers of another Duterte presidency -- whether by election or a forceful power grab.

Today, their ploy is to trigger the military. Deception and fake news after another, seeded carefully to sow distrust within the ranks. Was this perhaps the true agenda behind her visit to Senator Rodante Marcoleta in the Senate, accompanied by other Duterte-bloc senators? The timing was no accident. She did this on the same day Speaker Martin Romualdez was eased down from the speakership, a clear attempt to capitalize on perceived “cracks” within the administration.

Senate Blue Ribbon Committee

Marcoleta introduced a supposed “witness”, Orly Regala Gestuza, who claimed to have damning knowledge implicating Romualdez. Yet almost immediately, the entire spectacle collapsed under the weight of its own lies. The sworn affidavit he brandished was exposed as fake, with the very notary public, Atty. Petchie Rose Espera, categorically denying having notarized it. What was designed to be a bombshell against Romualdez became a humiliating implosion.

And yet, the Dutertes never stop at failure -- they weaponize it. Bato dela Rosa, ever the loyal soldier turned political operator, attempted to salvage the fiasco by harping on Gestuza’s supposed Marine background. Just right before the hearing concluded. A Plan B narrative. This was no random detail. It was a deliberate narrative play: if the public believed a “Marine” was disrespected or silenced, then the dignity of the entire Marine Corps would be dragged into the propaganda war. In one stroke, they sought to pit the people against the administration while sowing suspicion within the armed forces themselves. Only that of course they forget, Orly Regala Gusteza retired from service in 2020. His engagements after that are all private, as a civilian, and his actions does not represent anymore the virtues of an active-duty, loyal soldier of the Republic of the Philippines. It's best to delineate and leave the Philippine Marine Corp out of this mess.

But of course, the playbook does not end there. Knowing their witness has been discredited, the Duterte camp may very well stage something darker: the possibility of eliminating Orly Gestuza himself. An “assassination attempt,” pinned on the Romualdez camp, would suddenly transform a liar into a “martyr.” This tactic is not new, it is classic Duterte theater, where human lives are expendable so long as they serve political survival.

Behind this machination lurks the shadow of Mike Defensor. His name is synonymous with fake witnesses and fabricated testimony, dating back to the sordid days of Ador Mawanay in 2001. His fingerprints are all over these schemes, and his proximity to Vic Rodriguez, the disgraced former executive secretary of PBBM, shows that the Duterte machinery is not just vengeful, but carefully embedding itself with opportunists inside and outside the current administration.

This is the Duterte playbook: lies, fake witnesses, manipulation of institutions, the military dragged into partisan games, and the ever-present threat of violence. And at the center of it all is Sara Duterte, a vengeful politician consumed not by the welfare of the Filipino people, but by her burning desire to destroy anyone she perceives as an enemy.
